column4: The verse says God takes people by night, knows what they earn by day, then raises them; this gives the section's night/day distinction a human rhythm of hidden rest, visible action, and return.
God extends the shadow and makes the sun an indicator over it; this supplies a concrete nearby image of a layer spreading and daylight marking its reach, like the section's cover and disclosure.
After 25:45's extended shadow and sun as its indicator, this verse says God draws the shadow back gradually; its own contribution is the reverse motion from covering toward exposure.
This verse layers darkness over darkness, so a person can scarcely see his hand; it gives the section's cover-over-sight image a concrete scene of obscured vision, contrasted with opened daylight.

The verse says the earth will split open (“تَشَقَّقُ ٱلْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ”) and people will emerge; the source section's secondary dictionary form for النهار pictures a river splitting earth, and this makes opening ground reveal what it held.
On the Day, sight is dazzled (“بَرِقَ ٱلْبَصَرُ”); this marks the limit of the section's ordinary daylight image, since final disclosure can overwhelm sight.
After 75:7's dazzled sight, this verse says the moon is eclipsed (“خَسَفَ ٱلْقَمَرُ”); its own contribution is a reversal of the visible luminary that ordinarily distinguishes night and day.
Following the darkened moon in 75:8, this verse says sun and moon are joined (“جُمِعَ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ”); it collapses the distinction on which the section's paired scene depends.

The verse says clear proofs have come and that whoever sees does so for himself while the blind bears the loss; it makes explicit the section's concern that disclosure is available but can be refused.

This verse says that on that Day people will be exposed and no hidden thing will remain hidden (“لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ”); it is a direct final-day counterpart to night concealing and day making distinctions visible.

The verse says the heavens and earth were joined and then split apart (“فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا”); beside the source section's secondary dictionary image of النهار as a river splitting earth, it offers a cosmic opening that releases created life.

The source section's secondary dictionary form says a river splits the earth; here Moses strikes a rock and springs burst from it (“فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا”), a related opening-and-release image, though the verse has a rock rather than a river-cut ground.

The verse sets fasting's night against the first distinguishable dawn light (“حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلْخَيْطُ ٱلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْطِ ٱلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ”); like the section, it uses dawn to make a boundary emerge from darkness.

The source section links the word-family of 92:20's “face” to the dictionary phrase for the first face of day; this verse's “لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ” uses that word-family for the aim of giving, echoing the section's face as an orientation of purpose.

This verse describes people seeking their Lord's face (“يَبْتَغُونَ وَجْهَ رَبِّهِمْ”) and giving secretly and openly; it echoes the source section's face-word link while placing hidden and manifest action side by side.

The verse says the earth shines with its Lord's light (“وَأَشْرَقَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا”) as the record is set out; it stages final disclosure through light, making the section's opening-day image an eschatological scene.
